  SELECT json_agg(json_build_object(
    'qty', i.qty, 'price', i.price))
  FROM order_items i
  WHERE i.order_id = o.id
    AND i.price < 10) AS small
FROM orders o
WHERE o.id = 'o4';

SELECT o.id, (
  SELECT json_agg(json_build_object(
    'name', p.name,
    'cost', i.qty * i.price))
  FROM order_items i
  JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product
  WHERE i.order_id = o.id) AS lines
FROM orders o
WHERE o.id = 'o1';

SELECT order_id AS id,
       sum(qty) AS units,
       sum(qty * price) AS value
FROM order_items
GROUP BY order_id
ORDER BY order_id
LIMIT 2;

rows.sql:
SELECT o.id,
  (SELECT json_agg(f) FROM (
     SELECT qty FROM order_items
     WHERE order_id = o.id
     ORDER BY position
     LIMIT 1) f) AS first,
  (SELECT json_agg(r) FROM (
     SELECT qty FROM order_items
     WHERE order_id = o.id
     ORDER BY position
     OFFSET 1) r) AS rest
FROM orders o
WHERE o.id = 'o1';

SELECT o.id, (
  SELECT json_agg(
    json_build_object('qty', qty)
    ORDER BY qty DESC)
  FROM order_items
  WHERE order_id = o.id) AS by_qty
FROM orders o
WHERE o.id = 'o4';

rows.feature: Insert the rows of a query
rows.note: `insert` takes rows written out in the statement. A query's rows cannot be written to a collection.

rows.feature: One statement that inserts, updates and deletes by a join
rows.note: `upsert` covers insert-or-replace. Anything more is separate statements in a `transaction` block.
rows.sql:
MERGE INTO products p
USING incoming i ON p.id = i.id
WHEN MATCHED AND i.stock = 0 THEN
  DELETE
WHEN MATCHED THEN
  UPDATE SET stock = i.stock
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN
  INSERT VALUES (i.id, i.name,
    i.price, i.stock, i.category);

CREATE FUNCTION with_tax(
  amount float, rate float DEFAULT 0.5)
RETURNS float LANGUAGE sql AS
  $$ SELECT amount * (1 + rate) $$;
CREATE VIEW paid AS
  SELECT * FROM orders
  WHERE status = 'paid';

rows.feature: A failure undoes the whole block
rows.sql: ROLLBACK on error

rows.feature: A transaction held open across statements
rows.sql: BEGIN ... COMMIT over one connection
ROLLBACK

rows.feature: Two writers of one row cannot both win
rows.sql: serialization failure, row locks

rows.feature: Read-then-write in one statement is atomic
rows.sql: UPDATE ... SET n = n + 1

rows.feature: A commit that was acknowledged survives a crash
rows.sql: durability

rows.note: A transaction is kept whole or dropped whole.
One level: a transaction reads the database as of its start and is refused at commit if a row it changed was changed by another.
rows.sql:
BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL
  SERIALIZABLE;

rows.feature: Locking rows for a later write
rows.note: No row locks are taken by reads. A conflicting commit is refused and retried instead.
